# Pin labels in an app sidebar

Show the signed-in member's pinned workspace labels under an app's folder list, where one click opens the label's view through its label URL parameter: everything carrying the label, from every folder. Pins are personal; Mail is the reference.

1. The app needs a `label: uuid` parameter in `appViews` (`src/lib/app-view.ts`) and a list that answers by it. A label is a view, not a filter on the current folder (as in Gmail): Mail lists `?labelId=` without `?folder=` across the mailbox's folders in SQL (`ListLabeledMailPage`, `EXISTS` on `mail_tag`, Spam and Trash left out unless `includeSpamTrash=true`, the folder's paging and search); `?folder=` with `?labelId=` still narrows that folder. Contacts filter in SQL (`EXISTS` on `resource_label`), Chat and Calendar call `labels.Filter(ctx, w, source, labelId)` in the list handler, and Drive shows the labeled files of its whole listing, Trash excluded. Never filter only the visible page on the client when the route is paged.
2. Render `<PinnedLabels workspaceId app="<app>" value={view.label ?? ""} onChange={label => set({ label, folder: undefined, <open item>: undefined })} />` (`src/components/PinnedLabels.tsx`) inside the app's `AppSidebar`, under its folders; every folder button sets `label: undefined`, so clicking away clears the label. In a label view the title and the phone switcher (`AppSidebar current`) name the label, the active label is highlighted and no folder is, and each row names its folder (Mail's `.mail-folder-chip`, Drive's folder under the file name) since the view mixes folders. Actions update the view: a move to Spam or Trash, or removing the label, drops the row; an archive keeps it with its new folder. Opening a label, pinned or from the label select (`ResourceLabelFilter` with `pinApp`, which offers the pin checkbox), pushes a history entry, so Back returns to the folder. Call `useLabelGuard(workspaceId, labelId, onLost)` so a deleted label leaves the URL with a notice.
3. Pins are `label_pin` rows of the signed-in subject in the workspace (`internal/labels/pins.go`): `app` is one app or `all`, `pinned=false` is an explicit unpin, and a system label (`mail_label.system_key`) is pinned by default in its app without a row. Use the routes under `/api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/label-pins`; a label of another workspace is a 404. Settings → Labels holds a checkbox per app.
4. Test it: a Go test for any new list filter (another workspace's label matches nothing), and an e2e spec at 390px and 1440px with labels and resources unique to the run, as `e2e/label-pins.spec.ts` and `e2e/label-views.spec.ts` (labeled items in two folders both show, a folder click leaves the label) does. Run `lidza check --json` and `lidza test --e2e`.
